findings.reason: without a control for case 2 the node can land a guard that provably cannot refuse, and the section's whole safety property — that removing the admission lock does not let a held request launch — would be unproven.
findings.text: §35's negative control covers case 1 only ("takes the admission lock in `hold` again, and the first case times out"); case 2 — the pass re-reads a held request and does not launch it — is the only arm that measures the deliverable's second sentence, and nothing shows it can fail: a worker can add a phase re-read that never fires (or interleave the hold after the pass has already read `queued`, so the request is never in the launch set at all, `queue_admission.py:3945`) and all three cases still pass

response_events.note: §35 adds a second negative control: removing the pre-launch phase re-read makes the second case launch the held request, with the hold written after the pass has read it as queued
